summary.headline: Two Chaldaic Dodecaeterides
summary.text: Discussion of two Chaldaic twelve-year cycles (dodecaeterides), their predictions of weather, crop fertility, disease, and health, and their differing versions in Parisinus 2420 and Marcianus 324. The fuller version is dated to 996 but argued to preserve an older Augustan-era calendar through month names honoring Augustus, Agrippa, Livia, Octavia, Nero, Anchises, and Rome, with Hermann Usener cited on its historical institution.
